draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Karjat! Sitting about 100 km from both Mumbai and Pune on the Ulhas River, this town is one of the starting points for treks into the Western Ghats, including the climb to Rajmachi.
draft.hungryLine: Karjat keeps it simple, the small eateries around town and at the station will sort you out.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Take a rickshaw from Karjat Bridge to Kondivde or Khandpe village, the base of the Rajmachi trek.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Visit the farm fields around town, farming is the main way of life here and you can learn about the local culture.
moodReplies.surprise-me: At Kondhane Caves a big waterfall pours over the caves, and you can watch it from inside.

spots.name: Khandpe
spots.detail: Rickshaw from Karjat Bridge · The base village for the Rajmachi trek

spots.name: Kondhane Caves
spots.detail: On the Rajmachi trail · Caves behind a curtain of waterfall

spots.name: Rajmachi
spots.detail: 7 km climb from Khandpe · Base for the Manaranjan and Srivardhan forts

tips.title: Come in the rainy season.
tips.body: That's when Karjat's waterfalls are at their best.

tips.title: Take a rickshaw to the trailhead.
tips.body: From Karjat Bridge, ride to Kondivde, then it's a 15 minute walk to Khandpe.

story.title: Forts on the ridge
story.body: Above Rajmachi village stand two forts, Manaranjan (also called Manoranjan) and Srivardhan, with a lake and a temple.

story.title: A farming town
story.body: Farming is a major occupation around Karjat, with green plains rising into hilly terrain.

story.title: A growing town
story.body: The 2011 census counted 29,663 people in Karjat, with literacy above the state average.

story.title: Gateway to the Ghats
story.body: Karjat is part of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, run by a Municipal Council, and a favourite starting point for trekkers.
